RecordKey: one hundred and sixty-one thousand and forty
Content: @Matthew, the Bonferroni correction is not equivalent to multiplying the observed p-value by the number of comparisons. That would quickly lead to adjusted p-values >1, which is non-sensical. Instead, you *divide* alpha (typically .05) by the number of comparisons. Eg, if you want to adjust for 5 comparisons, you would use .05/5 = .01 as your new threshold for 'significance'.

Content: No, the bold part of that statement is not correct. (As a counterexample, consider repeating an experiment in which $n\\gt 1$ iid Normal$(0,1)$ values are drawn and the usual (symmetric Student t two-sided) confidence interval for the mean is constructed.
